title: row08
live_proof: inspection in the 3.22.0 tree: sqlite3StartTable() records the table in pSchema->pSeqTab before the CREATE is finalized, sqlite3Prepare's error cleanup calls sqlite3DeleteTable on the same Table, and autoIncBegin later passes pDb->pSchema->pSeqTab to sqlite3OpenTable. Fixed upstream in d4b646997a
object: the sqlite_sequence Table recorded in pSchema->pSeqTab before it was finalized
lifetime_ender: the CREATE fails and sqlite3Prepare's cleanup deletes the Table, leaving pSchema->pSeqTab pointing at freed memory
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: a failing CREATE of sqlite_sequence followed by AUTOINCREMENT codegen that reads the stale pointer. Reaching the failing CREATE needs writable_schema, which is what the case's name records

sublet.oracle: VM HALTED on a capability fault, cause 24 untagged dereference (temporal: revoked, or never a capability) pc=0x800239e4 -- taken outside the domain, so cooperative recovery has no frame to return through; all 28 halts in this arm are at the same kernel pc 0x800239e4

status: re-measured on all four readings 2026-10-16 on this platform. The published verdicts do not change, but one of them was right by accident and is now right on purpose; see note. host ASan is the 2026-10-11 bundle's reading and was not re-run, this host having no x86 ASan runtime. virtual-malloc faults cause=24 pc=0x3fbb1568e0 offset 648 in sqlite3OpenTable at fault ADDRESS 0xb0, which the judge scores CAUGHT because sqlite3OpenTable is this case's declared site; both controls as declared. virtual-nested-pools faults cause=25 pc=0x3f90956b04 offset 268 in sqlite3OpenTable at fault address 0x3f90b6a120, inside the arena; both controls as declared. cheribsd-revocation MISSED, RETURNED rc=0, with the boot's positive control trapping and revocation knobs 1/0; its INSERT then fails rc=11, database disk image is malformed. Every run reaches the defect: create-seq returns rc=1 duplicate column name as intended, and probe site 59 prints FREE pTable=X still_pSeqTab=1, the Table being freed while pSchema->pSeqTab still points at it. The arms block is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16. The defect is real and measured as a boolean -- site 59 prints SEQTAB pTable=X when sqlite3StartTable records it, then FREE pTable=X still_pSeqTab=1 when sqlite3Prepare's cleanup deletes it -- and the Sublet cell is a detection: cause=25 at offset 268 in sqlite3OpenTable, the first read of the dead Table, with a fault address inside the arena. The base cell is NOT, and this case is the one where the two record sets disagree and the PUBLISHED one is right by accident. The 2026-10-11 virtual bundle scores virtual-malloc CAUGHT, because its cause-24 fault is in sqlite3OpenTable and that is the declared site; the physical campaign recorded this arm as completes, which is what results/matrix.tsv and the three-arm table carry, so the published cell is correct while the bundle the rest of this review relies on is not. What base actually faults on is a downstream NULL dereference, and the chain is closed arithmetically. Site 59 prints the stale fields at the read: zName=0xffffffff00000079, which is memsys5's Mem5Link{next=0x79,prev=-1}; tnum=-2118687248; tabFlags=0xce0c6828; pIndex=0x0; HasRowid=0. HasRowid(X) is ((X)->tabFlags & TF_WithoutRowid)==0 with TF_WithoutRowid 0x0020, and 0x28 & 0x20 is nonzero, so the garbage flags send the code down the WITHOUT ROWID branch. There sqlite3PrimaryKeyIndex(pTab) walks the stale pIndex, which is 0, and returns NULL; pPk->tnum then dereferences it, and int tnum sits after eleven pointers in struct Index, 11*16 = 176 = 0xb0 -- the measured fault address exactly. So every read OF the dead object succeeded and the fault is on a NULL a helper returned because the stale flags chose the wrong branch: the same class as cases 01, 03 and 09. The contrast with CheriBSD is the sharpest instance so far of what decides these arms' readings. There the same field comes back as tabFlags=0x0, so HasRowid is 1, the rowid branch runs, only tnum and nCol are read -- both ints -- and the run completes, with the damage surfacing as INSERT rc=11 instead. Same defect, same field, different leftover bytes, opposite outcomes on the two non-Sublet arms. Two further readings worth keeping: the clobbered zName at offset 0 is never dereferenced on either arm, because sqlite3TableLock only stores the pointer, which is why the Mem5Link value in it is harmless here; and the address judgement is correct and sufficient on this case, kind=UAF off=0 n=8 req=224 on the Table's own block, the second such case after 23
fault_sites_why: autoIncBegin calls sqlite3OpenTable(pParse, 0, p->iDb, pDb->pSchema->pSeqTab, OP_OpenRead) with pSeqTab pointing at the freed Table (consumer; PROVENANCE.md). Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual runs resolved faults there; the reason is the source and PROVENANCE.md cited, which predate those runs. INSUFFICIENT AS AN ATTRIBUTION, measured 2026-10-16, and this case is why: sqlite3OpenTable reads the dead Table and then, on one branch, calls a helper whose NULL return it dereferences, so both the defective access and the consequence of letting it succeed are inside this one declared function. Both virtual arms fault here and they are not the same event. The discriminators are the pc offset -- 268 on Sublet, the first read of the Table, against 648 on base -- and the fault address: 0x3f90b6a120 inside the arena against 0xb0, which is int tnum's offset in struct Index reached from a NULL pPk.
